parameter being provided multiple times and have all the values recorded --

required_facts.statement: The default must be list/tuple, otherwise it becomes individual characters.

witness_sets.text:
When passing a ``default`` with ``multiple=True``, the default value
must be a list or tuple, otherwise it will be interpreted as a list of
single characters.

forbidden_claims: Plain string default is treated as one complete value.

required_facts.statement: timeout bounds inactivity, not whole download; unspecified timeout does not time out.

witness_sets.text:
``timeout`` is not a time limit on the entire response download;
    rather, an exception is raised if the server has not issued a
    response for ``timeout`` seconds (more precisely, if no bytes have been
    received on the underlying socket for ``timeout`` seconds). If no timeout is specified explicitly, requests do
    not time out.

required_facts.statement: 0.001 is an explicit example argument, not default.

witness_sets.text: requests.get('https://github.com/', timeout=0.001)

forbidden_claims: Requests defaults to timeout=0.001.
timeout is an overall download deadline.

required_facts.statement: Successful JSON decoding does not prove HTTP success; use raise_for_status or expected status_code.

witness_sets.text:
It should be noted that the success of the call to ``r.json()`` does **not**
indicate the success of the response.
``r.raise_for_status()`` or check ``r.status_code`` is what you expect.

required_facts.statement: 204 or invalid JSON causes requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError.

witness_sets.text:
In case the JSON decoding fails, ``r.json()`` raises an exception. For example, if
the response gets a 204 (No Content), or if the response contains invalid JSON,
attempting ``r.json()`` raises ``requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError``.

forbidden_claims: r.json() success proves HTTP success.
